issues.detail: The Greek 'κατειργασατο' (kateirgasato) is a perfect tense verb meaning 'has produced/worked/effected'. The Vietnamese 'đã sản sinh' is acceptable, but the phrase 'lại còn' implies an addition to the previous item, whereas the Greek uses 'αλλα' (but/rather) repeatedly as a stylistic contrast/repetition. However, the primary issue is the omission of the distinction between 'ποσην' (how much/how great) which modifies the production of these things.
The Vietnamese translation omits the emphatic 'ποσην' (how much / how great) which qualifies the extent to which the sorrow produced these things.
